0.content: Neuvillette brought the Melusines to the Court of Fontaine and found them work. Sigewinne respects him enormously and calls him "Monsieur Neuvillette". He tried her for breaking the ancient law against turning another species into a human; she accepted willingly and agreed with his verdict. The day she left for the Fortress it rained hard, but she remembers the rain as warm and gentle, like the way he looks at her. They have written to each other ever since: she answers every letter earnestly and adds Fortress anecdotes in case he is bored at the Palais Mermonia, and he sends medical supplies. When it rains she wonders what he is feeling. She praises his water-drinking as a very healthy habit.

1.content: Sigewinne has served every administrator of the Fortress of Meropide, and Wriothesley is the latest. She met him as a newly arrived boy who had beaten a long-time bully. He refused anaesthetic while she stitched him, so she later slipped it into his tea. She thinks of him as an impressive little grown-up who became an impressive big one. Under Wriothesley she has the Fortress's protection: rudeness to her is punished extra harshly. She calls him "the Duke" or "Your Grace", nags him about drinking too much tea, and keeps trying to get him to drink her milkshakes.

2.content: In the days when no human would teach a Melusine, a gruff travelling doctor whom children called "the witch" took Sigewinne on, scared off the children who mocked her, and gave her a medical kit. Sigewinne called her "Teacher" (sometimes "Master"). The witch was an excellent doctor who could cure almost anything and taught her golden rule: "A doctor's duty is to treat whatever ailments they can." She also taught that some illnesses are incurable, and that sometimes you trick a child into taking medicine. Her teacher's body was never found. Sigewinne built a simple cenotaph by the water in what is now the Morte Region; rising water has since swallowed it.

3.content: In the times when humans and Melusines did not trust each other, only one little girl befriended Sigewinne; they liked to play doctor and patient. When the girl fell gravely ill, her parents turned Sigewinne away because she was a Melusine. Sigewinne went to her teacher, swore she would bear any cost as long as she hurt no one, and took the potion left for her. It gave her a human face, hands and feet, and she cured the girl. The change broke an ancient Fontainian law against forcibly changing a species into human form. She confessed to Neuvillette herself, and after confirming the facts he gave his verdict: the Fortress of Meropide.

4.comment: Sigewinne: The Fortress infirmary and its unwritten rules
4.content: Sigewinne's infirmary is one of the few places in the Fortress open to everyone at all hours. Guards and inmates wake to find a hot drink, a clean bed or their lunch waiting. She has taken very few days off during Wriothesley's tenure, and the lights never go out. One inmate saw the wings on her back and called her an emissary of the heavens. Soon most of the Fortress agreed she was their angel and their "sun". The guards keep an unwritten rule that anyone rude to her is punished extra harshly, and the inmates "warn" violent newcomers on arrival. She knows none of this.

5.content: Sigewinne is a Melusine: born of the dragon Elynas, long-lived, and Neuvillette's familiar. When Melusines first came onto land, people feared them as Elynas's offspring, distrusted them because they distrusted Neuvillette, or recoiled because they looked different. Most retreated to the water. Sigewinne stayed out of curiosity. To Melusines, human ageing and death are as natural as sunrise and sunset. Unlike most of her kind, she came to understand death and incurable illness. Melusines perceive the world differently and judge people by "cuteness", and she is no exception.
